elements.markdown: The trace shows **900 ms on the server**, including **620 ms in repeated per-account queries**, followed by **350 ms rendering 2,000 rows**. We can work on SQL and the frontend together. Billing must stay fresh after edits, search must cover every row, and adding infrastructure is outside the current scope.

elements.multi: Which improvements should we explore together?

options.description: Targets the largest measured cost; query plans will help identify a safe SQL change.
Targets the 350 ms browser cost; changes navigation or rendering behavior.
Summary reporting may lag up to 30 seconds; introduces invalidation and stale-data tradeoffs.

Batch account queries.text: Proposed approach: inspect the query plan, replace repeated per-account reads with a batched query where appropriate, and compare timing and returned data. Keep the billing edit/read path immediately fresh.

Render fewer table rows.select: Which table approach should we investigate?

options.description: Check keyboard navigation and full-data search before choosing a rendering change.
Renders one page at a time; users navigate between pages and search still covers all rows.
Renders visible rows while scrolling; needs care for keyboard navigation and accessibility.

Virtual scrolling.input: Any table interactions we must preserve?
Virtual scrolling.placeholder: For example: keyboard navigation, browser find, selection, or copying rows

Reuse summary results briefly.text: Investigate reuse within the existing application. Billing reads after edits must bypass stale results or invalidate them; no new infrastructure is proposed.
